17.description: The committee recommends reallocating $4 million to integrate advanced water treatment for taste, odor, and hydrocarbon removal into the new water treatment plant, expected by 2032.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Residents could face water restrictions if a major hydrocarbon spill occurs before 2032.
Funds will integrate powder activated carbon for hydrocarbon removal in the new plant.
Administration will engage a consultant to design an upstream water monitoring program.

18.description: Saskatoon City Council approved noise bylaw extensions for four special events in 2026, including Pride, Outskirts, Hudson's Block Party, and Rock the River, allowing later noise.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Administration lacks resources for real-time noise complaint response.
Residents near River Landing, Sasktel Centre, 4th Avenue, and Rotary Park are affected.
Council requested review of noise bylaw guidelines for standardized reporting.
Public awareness of noise complaint feedback routes remains unclear.
Delegates supported Rock the River, Outskirts Music Festival, and Hudson's Block Party.
Administration will explore costs for real-time noise monitoring if needed.

20.description: The committee recommends renaming a waste reserve to the Waste Utility Capital Reserve, consolidating $5.1 million, and expanding its use for all waste collection capital needs, including diversion efforts. This has no direct immediate impact on residents.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Davies questioned if the reserve change would negatively impact waste diversion efforts.
Utility rates may be adjusted in 2028 to cover lost funding for waste programs.
New reserve funds initiatives for 70% waste diversion target and climate action plan.
Staff committed to maintaining the 70% waste diversion target and refreshing the diversion plan.

9.description: Council received several information reports, including one responding to a May 2018 Council Resolution.

chips.text: Received as information
6 for, 0 against

19.description: Saskatoon will not proceed with a non-potable irrigation pilot project in Brighton's La Palaz Park due to high costs and operational complexities, but will explore options in other new developments.

chips.text: The proposed pump house for the system would cost an estimated $675,000.
The project aimed to reduce potable water use and greenhouse gas emissions.
Administration will explore non-potable irrigation in Holwood and University Heights 3.

21.description: Saskatoon partners with the Saskatoon Tribal Council on an Indigenous apprenticeship program in Fleet Services, training heavy duty mechanics and fostering a culturally safe workplace. The program aims to expand to other city departments.

chips.text: Councillor Parker questioned the report's "word salad" on cultural conditions for apprentices.
Two Indigenous apprentices launched the program in March 2021.
This is the city's first Indigenous apprenticeship program.
Saskatoon Tribal Council is "very impressed and pleased" with the partnership.
Aims to remove systemic barriers and create employment pathways for Indigenous peoples.
Indigenous Workplace Specialist will conduct regular check-ins with apprentices.
